entries.topic: US deaths and costs from Hezbollah, the Iraqi militias and the Houthis

claims.text: 18 April 1983 suicide truck bombing of the US Embassy in Beirut killed 63 people, including 17 Americans, 8 of them CIA officers; the Islamic Jihad Organization, which the CIA says later became part of Hizballah, claimed it

Marine barracks bombing 23 October 1983 killed 241 US servicemen (plus 58 French troops at a second site); Peterson v. Iran (Lamberth, 30 May 2003) found Hezbollah carried it out with 'massive material and technical support' from Iran and that Iran and MOIS 'played crucial and necessary roles in planning and ordering' it; Anderson (2010) restated these findings [audit: the "crucial and necessary roles" sentence is the Anderson (2010) court's own finding, not a quotation from Peterson; "formed under the auspices of the government of Iran" is from Peterson, quoted in Anderson n.4]

Islamic Jihad claimed the barracks bombing; Hezbollah officially denied involvement and Hezbollah, Iran and Syria have continued to deny it; Iran did not answer the families' suit; Lamberth awarded about $2.66bn in 2007; the US Supreme Court ruled in April 2016 frozen Iranian central-bank assets could pay; Reagan ordered withdrawal 7 Feb 1984, completed 26 Feb 1984

TWA 847 hijacked 14 June 1985 (Athens–Rome); US Navy diver Robert Stethem, 23, killed 15 June and his body thrown onto the tarmac; hostages released 30 June; US indicted Imad Mughniyeh, Hassan Izz-al-Din and Ali Atwa, described as linked to Hezbollah, with a $5m reward; Hezbollah denied any link

CIA Beirut station chief William Buckley seized 16 March 1984; Islamic Jihad announced 4 Oct 1985 it had executed him; the NSC said he probably died 3 June 1985; remains found 27 December 1991 near Beirut airport; Nov 1985 arms-for-hostages contacts sought release of Americans held in Lebanon

Costs of War (Oct 2024): FY2024 US regional operations costs $4.86bn: $2.4bn from the April 2024 Israel supplemental for US operations, force protection and deterrence in CENTCOM's region; $2.4bn additional carrier groups and actions against the Houthis; $55–70m combat pay; Navy had fired about $1bn of munitions in the Red Sea by June 2024; carrier strike group ~$8.7m a day

April 2024 supplemental for Israel: $14.1bn incl. $4bn Iron Dome and David's Sling, $1.2bn Iron Beam, $3.5bn FMF, $1bn artillery/munitions production, $4.4bn replenishment of US stocks; with the $3.8bn annual allotment $17.9bn

Two US service members were lost in January 2024 during an operation that seized Iranian-made missiles on a vessel bound for Yemen; Military Times counted at least 217 incidents involving US forces in the region since October 2023

Costs of War (Oct 2025): US military operations in the wider Middle East Oct 2023–Sep 2025 cost $9.65–12.07bn excluding aid to Israel; $31.35–33.77bn including $21.7bn military aid; FY2025 Houthi/Yemen operations $2.76–4.95bn (Rough Rider carriers $2.27–4.36bn; munitions $0.23–0.31bn incl. 1,000–1,500 2,000-lb bombs, 75+ Tomahawks; three F/A-18s lost ~$210m); 40,000–43,000 US troops in region; CENTCOM 41% of carrier steaming days in 2025 vs 8% the year before

Costs of War (Oct 2025): Midnight Hammer/June 2025 Iran costs $2.04–2.25bn, incl. THAAD interceptors defending Israel $1.8–1.95bn (~150 fired, about a quarter of stock), B-2 $76–108m, 14 GBU-57 $49–70m, Tomahawks $36–46m, Patriots defending Al Udeid ~$57m

entries.topic: The June 2025 strikes and the 2026 Iran war: decision, Congress, casualties, oil, polling

claims.text: Cato's Hoffman: Netanyahu backed toppling Saddam in 2002 testimony to Congress; Olmert sought Bush's approval to bomb Iran in 2008, refused; per Netanyahu's memoir he asked Obama in 2013 to strike Iran, declined; 2015 address to Congress against the JCPOA; Trump reportedly complained Netanyahu was 'willing to fight Iran to the last American soldier'; argues Netanyahu has domestic incentives to widen conflict

House of Commons Library: US and Israel began strikes 28 Feb 2026 stating aims of regime change and targeting Iran's nuclear and ballistic-missile programmes; US said its actions were self-defence; Iran said it would shut the Strait of Hormuz; 'almost all shipping has ceased'; US counter-blockade from 13 April; IEA members released 400 million barrels; conditional ceasefire 8 April; UK did not join strikes

AP (18 Jul 2026): 16 US service members dead: 6 soldiers in Kuwait from an Iranian drone at a civilian port shortly after 28 Feb; 1 at Prince Sultan AB after a 1 March Iranian attack; 6 in a KC-135 crash in Iraq in March (not described as hostile); 1 Navy pilot in a 1 July Arabian Sea helicopter crash; 2 in Jordan 18 July defending against Iranian missiles and drones

Intercept (28 Sep 2026): official Pentagon count of 880 dead or wounded, 444 after the administration declared Epic Fury concluded on 7 July; about 100 in September; at least 19 dead (11 hostile) per official count; Intercept calls the tally an undercount; Hegseth called a WaPo report of suppressed numbers 'DISGUSTING and FAKE'

Quinnipiac 6–8 Mar 2026 (1,002 RV, ±3.8): 53% oppose, 40% support US military action against Iran (R 85–11 support; I 60–31 oppose; D 89–7 oppose); 74% oppose ground troops; 55% say Iran did not pose an imminent military threat (83% D, 63% I)

PBS/AP summary (March 2026): Fox News poll split evenly on the action and about 6 in 10 say Iran poses a real national security threat; about 7 in 10 concerned about oil and gas prices (Quinnipiac); CNN snap poll about half think strikes make Iran more of a threat

Reuters/Ipsos (late July 2026, 1,246 adults): about one in three support the war (27% on day one, 37% mid-March); 69% say Trump has not clearly explained the goals, incl. four in 10 Republicans; gas just over $4 a gallon vs about $3 before 28 Feb

15 July 2026: House rejected Massie amendment to bar Israel funding in the FY2027 State/national-security appropriations bill, eliminating about $3.3bn FMF, 104 yes–314 no–10 present per CBS/FMEP (The New Arab gives 103, which omits Massie); Massie the only Republican yes; Jeffries called it 'overly broad'; Clark and Pelosi voted yes

Senate 27 June 2025 rejected motion to discharge Kaine's S.J.Res. 59 (Iran war powers after June 2025 strikes) 47–53 (taken from the Sophia 2026 Elections key-vote dataset; roll call not re-fetched this session)

House agreed H.Con.Res. 86 (WPR s.5(c) concurrent resolution directing removal of US forces from hostilities with Iran) 215–208 on 3 June 2026 (4 R yes); Senate agreed 50–48 on 23 June 2026; concurrent resolution not presented to the President and its legal force disputed; administration opposed (from Sophia 2026 Elections key-vote dataset; roll calls not re-fetched this session)

Midnight Hammer began 21 June 2025 (US time) after Israel's 13 June 'Rising Lion' strikes; struck Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan; table lists 7 B-2 units, 14 GBU-57s and 24 Tomahawks; Iran struck Al Udeid in response after notifying the US; at least 14 Patriot interceptors fired; no US deaths reported in this period

entries.topic: The 2026 war decision and stated reasons (existing keys)

claims.text: Wikipedia's compilation of reporting: in early 2026 Netanyahu lobbied Trump for a joint strike targeting Iran's leadership; Trump authorized Epic Fury on 27 Feb (Air Force One); reporting cites Israeli intelligence provided by Netanyahu as a decisive factor; nuclear talks were ongoing in February until strikes began; Trump's 28 Feb statement cited Iran's support for Hamas and Hezbollah, protester killings, attacks on US citizens and soldiers, and the 1979 hostage crisis

Wikipedia: Hormuz shipping slowed to a standstill around 1 March 2026 with about 150 ships stalled; described as the largest supply disruption in the oil market's history; US official counts cited there: 19 soldiers and 1 contractor killed

NPR (28 Feb 2026): Trump said the aim was to eliminate 'imminent threats from the Iranian regime'; told Iranians 'When we are finished, take over your government'; claimed Iran was rebuilding its nuclear programme though the IAEA said it had no evidence Iran had resumed enrichment; Netanyahu: 'remove the existential threat posed by the terrorist regime in Iran'

entries.topic: Verification: Iran war-powers votes 2025-2026, April 2024 Israel supplemental, Pew/Gallup polls, Netanyahu's role in the 2026 decision

claims.text: AP: Senate on Friday 27 June 2025 rejected Kaine's Iran war-powers measure 53-47 (i.e. 47 in favour, 53 against) - figure confirmed
House passed Iran war-powers resolution 215-208 on 3 June 2026, four Republicans (Fitzpatrick, Barrett, Davidson, Massie) in favour; Trump called it 'a meaningless vote'
Senate adopted H.Con.Res. 86 50-48 on 23 June 2026; Republicans Cassidy, Collins, Murkowski and Paul in favour, Fetterman against, McConnell and McCormick not voting

Concurrent resolution does not go to the President; White House official: 'Concurrent resolutions do not go to the president and have no force of law', said hostilities 'terminated with the ceasefire on April 7th'; Trump called it 'poorly timed and meaningless'; a House Democratic aide argued it was binding
24 September 2026 Senate rejected an Iran war-powers resolution 49-50; the Senate had voted 14 times and passed only the June measure; Cassidy later reverted to no after an administration briefing

Israel Security Supplemental Appropriations Act 2024 totals $26.38bn: $4bn Iron Dome/David's Sling, $1.2bn Iron Beam, $3.5bn FMF, $1bn artillery/critical munitions, $4.4bn to replenish US articles provided to Israel, $2.4bn for current US military operations in the region
The $26bn package included over $9bn humanitarian aid for Gaza and elsewhere; House vote 366-58 on 20 April 2024
Pew 16-22 March 2026 (3,524 adults): 59% said US made wrong decision using force in Iran, 38% right; 61% disapprove Trump's handling; 88% of Democrats wrong decision, 71% of Republicans right
Gallup 1-15 June 2026: about 34-35% approved of US military action in Iran, lower than most US military operations since the 1980s (as reported by FOX 29)

Reuters (three people briefed, anonymous): Netanyahu phoned Trump within 48 hours before the strikes and argued there might never be a better chance to kill Khamenei; Trump had already approved the idea of an operation but not timing; sources believed call and intelligence window helped prompt the 27 Feb order; Reuters could not determine its effect; White House did not address the call; Trump says decision his alone
19 March 2026 Netanyahu called claims Israel dragged the US into war 'fake news': 'Does anyone really think that someone can tell President Trump what to do?'

entries.topic: Audit re-verification: Massie amendment tally; Iran war status mid-October 2026

claims.text: Massie amendment (Amendment 8 to H.R. 8595, FY2027 State/national security appropriations), 15 July 2026: failed 104 yes, 314 no, 10 present; 103 Democrats and one Republican (Massie) voted yes; would have eliminated $3.3bn in assistance to Israel. The New Arab's total of 103 omits Massie's vote.

CBS (updated 13 Oct 2026): Iran's ports under US blockade since the ceasefire collapsed in July; CENTCOM: 4 vessels disabled and 135 turned around since the blockade took effect 14 July; Iran attacking ships in Hormuz; late September Iranian ceasefire proposal (lift shipping restrictions) publicly rejected by Trump while talks continue via mediators; Trump's previously announced decision not to strike Iran until after the midterms; asked about the Houthi Riyadh airport strike, 'Well, we're gonna take a look'; no direct US-Iran combat reported in the period
